checkboxes.description: ID parameter validated and 404 returned if tool not found

evidence.reasoning: The service method calls repository.update() directly without checking if the tool exists first. While Prisma will throw an error if the record doesn't exist (P2025), there's no explicit 404 handling like in the getDetailsById method which properly checks and throws NotFoundException

The GET endpoint properly validates existence and returns 404. The PUT endpoint lacks this explicit validation pattern, relying on Prisma's implicit error which may not return a proper 404 status code

While some fields like name, description, vendor, etc. are properly marked as optional with @IsOptional(), the presence of required fields means this is NOT a true partial update implementation

checkboxes.description: Response returns 200 OK with updated complete object

evidence.reasoning: Returns the complete updated tool object with all fields, including transformed monthly_cost. NestJS defaults to 200 OK status for successful PUT requests
Prisma's update() method returns the complete updated record by default, ensuring all fields are included in the response

reasoning: The PUT endpoint implementation has significant issues. While the endpoint exists with proper path parameter and body parsing (2/2 points), and returns the correct response format (1/1 points), it fails on three critical requirements. First, there is no explicit 404 validation before update - the service relies on Prisma's implicit error handling rather than checking existence and throwing NotFoundException like the GET endpoint does. Second, partial update is not properly supported because monthly_cost and status fields are marked as required with @IsNotEmpty(), forcing clients to provide these values even when they don't want to change them. Third, validation rules are completely duplicated between CreateToolDto and UpdateToolDto with no reuse mechanism. Total score: 3/8 points.
